quizzes.question: Why doesn't inflation affect everyone equally?
options: It only affects people who don't work hard enough
People who receive newly created money first benefit before prices rise; savers holding cash lose value in the meantime
Inflation actually affects everyone in exactly the same way

quizzes.question: According to this section, why does wealth inequality tend to widen under ongoing inflation?
options: Asset owners benefit as asset prices rise with the money supply, while wages for non-owners often lag behind
Poor people spend money less wisely than rich people
Inflation is designed specifically to punish asset owners

quizzes.question: What problem did earlier attempts at digital cash (before Bitcoin) fail to solve without relying on a trusted central party?
options: The double-spend problem — preventing the same digital money from being spent twice
Making digital money look visually appealing

quizzes.question: What is Proof-of-Work used for in Bitcoin?
options: It lets a central authority approve transactions faster
It makes it expensive to cheat and cheap to verify, allowing independent computers to agree on a shared history without a trusted party
It encrypts messages between users for privacy

quizzes.question: What enforces Bitcoin's maximum supply of 21 million coins?
options: A promise made by Satoshi Nakamoto personally
A vote held every four years among miners
The software rules that every participant on the network independently runs and verifies

quizzes.question: What tradeoff does this section highlight as often underestimated by new Bitcoin users?
options: Bitcoin transactions take several days to complete
Removing the need for a central authority also removes the safety net of a bank fixing your mistakes — personal responsibility increases
Bitcoin cannot be used for small purchases
